An undercurrent of the Maker movement --that most people seem to think is nothing but a DIY revival-- is an idea called 'unplugging'. It's the notion that one can leverage emerging open technology of industrial independence on improved community resilience and a whittling-away of market dependencies and hegemonies, and to achieve this without the sacrifices in standard of living that was previously assumed to require. We can't, realistically, homestead in the wilderness like our frontier ancestors without a great sacrifice in standard of living. But we don't need to go to that extreme to have a significant economic impact. And there is a great deal more we can do than people realize. Many Makers envision a near-future where tools of industrial independence become a means to a new kind of early retirement where one turns one's home and community into an engine of comfortable subsistence.

The long-term trends in production are toward machines that are not only smarter but more flexible (making production capacity a commodity), shrinking in minimum production volumes toward manufacture-on-demand, shrinking in physical scale, and shrinking in cost. You can now initiate more kinds of production out of pocket than ever before and the number of things you can't competitively manufacture in the space of a 2-4 car garage is steadily shrinking. The upper-class is on an upper deck of the same sinking boat as the workers when it comes to automation because the technology is obsolescing both jobs AND capital. Consumer goods production volume in job shops passed that of traditional factories in 2000 and never went back. Most large 'manufacturers' no longer own their own production. The cost of money for that has become a competitive liability. There is a global entrepreneurial explosion going on right now empowered by this industrial de-massification. Disruption of markets and their hegemonies is often just a matter of design.

Did you know that Bitcoin was invented by the same community that created Linux, started the trend in fab labs, started the Maker movement, invented crowdfunding, and started the current desktop 3D printer craze? Did you know that same community has been developing all those open source microcontrollers now pioneering the Internet of Things, has been developing technology to turn homebuilding into a one-person proposition, and cultivating an open Global Village Toolkit to modernize subsistence farming around the world? Did you know they are even working on making automobile production something you can do on-demand at a dealership or in your own home? The earth is shifting right under our feet and most people haven't even noticed.
